teile.name: Blocked ad
teile.text: Congressmen asked CBS not to run this ad. Temu's giveaway ads still appeared. Why?

regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

Ensure every visual motif directly depicts the specific historical event, person, or technical workflow described in the narration at that exact second.
Avoid generic, ambient, or unrelated stock imagery; visual alignment must be precise to the historical or technical content.
Place the final call-to-action only after the narrative conclusion has been delivered, ensuring no instructional or summary text follows the CTA.
Anchor all chronological facts and dates strictly to the central narrative tension to maintain a fast, high-tempo storytelling pace.
Open every script with a curiosity-driven hook that establishes central tension before any early engagement requests.
Ensure the opening call-to-action is only placed after sufficient substantive context has been established.
Insert a mid-point narrative tease or fresh question every 40 to 60 seconds to re-engage attention.
Verify topic uniqueness to avoid repeating subjects unless a significant new angle or enough time has elapsed.
Maintain the channel identity of the specific presenter (fedora/suit for Business Origin Stories; leather jacket/cyan glasses for AI Tools Explained) in all visual scenes.
Match the visual style of historical or fictional scenes to original urban painted open-world-game aesthetics, avoiding copied game characters.
Use distinct, non-repetitive motifs that provide genuine evidence or illustrative detail, avoiding reliance on zooms, crops, or static loops as motif changes.
Explain human tasks and source-supported actions in AI tool segments rather than listing technical specifications, benchmarks, or architecture details.

story.besserer_hook: The final sentence should directly tie the ad campaign to the spike in users, e.g. "The ads drove a 100‑million user surge, proving the strategy worked."
schwaechen: The ending does not clearly answer the hook’s promise that the ads caused a surge in users; it merely states a statistic without showing the causal link.

belege.name: Temu
belege.text:
Temu (  TEM-oo, also   TEE-moo; originally short for "Team Up, Price Down") is a Chinese-owned online marketplace operated by e-commerce company PDD Holdings, which was founded by Chen Lei, Colin Huang, and Zhao Jiazhen. It offers heavily discounted consumer goods, mostly shipped to consumers directly from China. By April 2025, the platform had expanded its operations to more than 90 markets.
In March 2024, Temu launched its Local Seller Program in the United States. As of July 2025, the program was operational in the UK, France, Italy, Japan, Mexico, and Australia, among other countries. The program is designed to avoid tariffs in the USA and other countries.
Temu's business model has allowed it to become popular among consumers, but has also drawn concerns over data privacy, forced labor, intellectual property, and the low quality of its marketplace products. The company has been embroiled in legal disputes with Shein, a direct competitor. The rise of Temu is one of Amazon's biggest challenges in years. A 2023 report by the U.S. House Select Committee on Strategic Competition found an "extremely high risk" of forced labor in the company's supply chains and accused it of exploiting the U.S. de minimis trade loophole to evade customs enforcement. The platform has faced multiple class action lawsuits over data privacy practices, investigations by South Korean and European regulators over toxic substances in products and breaches of the Digital Services Act, and criticism from 
History: Temu is owned and operated by PDD Holdings, a multinational commerce group registered in the Cayman Islands with Dublin also listed as its principal office address. PDD Holdings also owns Pinduoduo, a popular online commerce platform in China. In the U.S., Temu is under the ownership of Whaleco, Inc., a subsidiary of PDD Holdings registered in the states of Delaware and Massachusetts.
The Temu platform first went live in the United States in September 2022, and ran ads during the February 2023 Super Bowl. In March 2023, Temu launched in Australia and New Zealand. In the following month, Temu launched in France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and the UK. Temu eventually expanded into the Latin American market. On January 17, 2024, Temu officially launched in South Africa, the 49th country that Temu had entered since its launch. As of the same month, U.S. MAUs on the app reached more than 51 million.
In February 2024, Temu offered US$15 million in giveaways in multiple Super Bowl ads that several congressmen had asked the CBS network not to run. As a result of the ads, the company saw a spike in searches for their name and traffic, reaching 100 million active users in the U.S., over 130 million app downloads globally, and approximately 420 million monthly website visits, as per Semrush. Research by Sensor Tower estimated that in the last quarter of 2023 Temu users spent an average of 23 minutes a week on the app, compared with 18 minutes on Amazon and 22 minutes on eBay.
As of March 2024, Temu served approximately 30 million daily users in America. By August, the number of users of the Temu app had reached 91% of that of Amazon. As of December of the same year, Temu.com saw nearly 700 million monthly visits.
In 2024, Temu introduced the Local Seller Program, opening its marketplace to local sellers in numerous markets. This program enables sellers in these countries to list their products directly and fulfill domestic orders. Through this program, both small businesses and individual entrepreneurs in America can connect directly with millions of customers.
Temu's appearance at the 2024 Super Bowl garnered significant exposure, which made it a household name for U.S. consumers.
In January 2025, International Post Corporation released the 2024 edition of the IPC Cross-Border E-Commerce Shopper Survey Report, which showed Temu overtaking AliExpress as the second most used e-retailer for cross-border sales in the world.
As of March 2025, Temu was one of the most widely used online shopping websites in America. In May, it entered into a partnership with the International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition. In July, the company joined the International Trademark Association and became a member of the Anti-Counterfeiting Committee of the Association.
